column11: ANCHOR, measured: 262 of 426 US patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who started concurrent chemoradiation, 61.5%, went on to consolidation durvalumab (Arunachalam A et al., PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314156, PMC11588217, US Oncology Network, starts 2017 to 2019); death (28.3%) and progression (22.2%) were the main reasons the rest did not. That is Imfinzi's own capture of this pool, the slot oleclumab would share. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 61.5% = 30.75% of each year's patients at peak. For: AstraZeneca owns the backbone and would move its own consolidation patients; in COAST the combination's PFS hazard ratio against durvalumab alone was 0.44 (Barlesi F et al., Future Oncol 2024, doi:10.1080/14796694.2024.2354160); and a rival add-on trial in this setting, PACIFIC-8 with domvanalimab, was discontinued for strategic portfolio prioritisation (appendix of 27 July 2026). Against: the monalizumab arm of the same trial could take the slot instead; a blinded Phase 3 effect is usually smaller than an open-label Phase 2 one; the combination adds infusions in the first two cycles; and Tagrisso's US label now covers EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III disease after chemoradiation (DailyMed, in the book's labels table), which takes those patients out of durvalumab consolidation after the 2017 to 2019 measurement
